workloads.name: one file x 413 (django/__init__.py, tests/admin_views/__init__.py, tests/admin_views/urls.py), cold

hypotheses.evidence: strace -c on full Django: futex 619.7 thread-s over only 6,039 waits (avg 103 ms); /usr/bin/time -v 358 voluntary context switches in 330 s. Few long parks of idle rayon workers, not many short contended waits.

hypotheses.claim: I/O or the store is a lever.
hypotheses.evidence: strace -c on full Django: read, pread64, statx, lseek, openat and write together under 9 thread-s of 2,636 CPU-s; 1,534,769 pread64 calls cost 3.3 thread-s.

hypotheses.claim: Parse and syntax facts are a CPU lever.
hypotheses.evidence: perf record --children on full Django: ParseContract::read_file_explicit 0.44%, derived structures 0.90%, cross-file 0.13%, spill and frontier storage 0.07%.

hypotheses.claim: Rule compilation and program preparation dominate.
hypotheses.evidence: perf record --children: compile_one 0.05% and PrepareUseCase::prepare 0.03% on full Django (31.3% and 22.2% on one file only).

hypotheses.claim: The per-file executor is the cost, and most of it is runtime around the kernels.
hypotheses.evidence: perf record --children on full Django: RequestExecution::run_file 99.2%; RegisteredOperator::evaluate 26.9%; the rest of prepare_roots about 68% (prepare_roots self 10.68%, Slot::touched 2.81%, inspect_available 2.37%).

hypotheses.claim: Most (file, rule) evaluations produce nothing for the file.
hypotheses.evidence: output coverage.evaluated 1,186,980 pairs on full Django, 2,507 with a finding: 99.79% of pairs report nothing. One-file split: about 0.46 CPU-s per near-empty file is program walk.

hypotheses.claim: Allocation churn in runtime bookkeeping is large.
hypotheses.evidence: jemalloc prof_accum with jeprof --alloc_objects on full Django: 5,939 M allocations, 2,650 GB; 39.8% under source admission publish, 34.1% under region evaluate; madvise 148,075 calls, 67 thread-s.

hypotheses.claim: The per-file slot table is a large share of per-file memory.
hypotheses.evidence: jeprof --cum on the one-file peak dump: Slot::touched (runtime/service/state/service.rs:25) 251.7 MB of 824.7 MB; 723.5 MB at 100 files; 587.2 MB in the full-Django peak.

levers.lever: Do not instantiate or walk rules that cannot match a file: decide from a cheap per-file necessary condition which rule roots run; untouched regions get no slot and no poll.
levers.evidence: 99.79% of 1,186,980 (file, rule) pairs report nothing (h6); executor 99.2% of full-Django CPU (h5); about 0.46 CPU-s per near-empty file is program walk.

levers.lever: Per-file runtime state proportional to work: dense slots for regions that run, a worker-local arena reused across files.
levers.evidence: Slot::touched table 251.7 MB one file, 723.5 MB at 100 files (h8); Slot::touched 2.8-4.0% self CPU; Invocation and AdmissionProgress drops 3-5%; 148,075 madvise calls.

levers.lever: Stream kernel output instead of buffering whole row sets per kernel.
levers.evidence: full-Django peak dump: kernel evaluation rows 1,240 MB (replay/types.rs:19 1,009 MB; lease.rs:265 879 MB; __rust_realloc 1,665 MB live).

levers.lever: Fuse rule passes so per-region runtime overhead is paid once per fused pass.
levers.evidence: runtime around kernels 68% of full-Django CPU, 82% at 100 files (h5).

levers.lever: Share the prepared program across workers instead of cloning it.
levers.evidence: Operation::clone at values/src/domain/plans/types.rs:44/46 holds 146 MB at the one-file peak; prepare 280 MB and compile 147 MB shared.

levers.lever: Close the idle 20% of worker time.
levers.evidence: futex 620 thread-s over 6,039 waits; 797% CPU on 10 cores (h1).
